title: General hom comparison cocycles
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified six operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Finite inputs used for compact support carry compatible etale-origin witnesses; integral inputs are derived complete with compatible witnessed finite reductions, rational operations are raw localization, and algebraically closed coefficients are represented at a common finite coefficient field. All operations below are restricted to their stated constructible domains; tensor factors and comparisons have their stated finite-Tor hypotheses. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and put $H_B(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_B(K,M)$ for derived internal Hom on its small pro-etale site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For $n\ge m\ge1$ and $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ write $K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$, likewise $M_m$, and let $v_{n,m}:H_{A_n}(K,M)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{A_m}(K_m,M_m)$ be the isomorphism of [thm-coef-finite-hom]: the unique tensor-Hom transpose of coefficient change of evaluation, with its successive-quotient equation $v_{n,r}=v_{m,r}\circ(v_{n,m}\otimes^L A_r)$ for $m\ge r\ge1$. For $K,M$ in the derived category of $R_X$-modules, $R_X=\lim_n(A_n)_X$, let $c_n:H_{R_X}(K,M)\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{A_n}(K_n,M_n)$ be the isomorphism of [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], the transpose of reduced evaluation, defined for arbitrary ambient variables. For finite extensions $E\subset E'$ use the integral scalar-extension Hom comparisons of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]. Then:
(1) $v_{n,n}=1$ under the identification $-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_n=\mathrm{id}$.
(2) For $n\ge m\ge1$ and integral $K,M$ whose reductions $K_n,M_n$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$, under the canonical successive tensor identifications,
$$c_m=v_{n,m}\circ(c_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m).$$
(3) Wherever the elementary coefficient comparison for internal Hom of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] is also defined (finite quotients with site-perfect first variable, integral-to-finite reduction, rationalization and common-stage scalar extension), it equals $v_{n,m}$, $c_n$, respectively the scalar-extension comparison.
(4) Consequently these comparisons, together with the scalar-extension comparisons, preserve evaluations and their tensor-Hom transposes and tensor reassociation, so every well-typed equation formed from these maps and from the identity and composition equations of the three cited statements is preserved; raw localization and common finite-stage passage preserve these equations on their constructible domains.
These assertions do not replace finite-Tor by site-perfectness, do not assert the site-perfect tensor-dual formula for arbitrary constructible objects, and do not introduce finite reduction of rational objects.

source.place: Agent-formulated sub-obligation for general internal Hom comparisons: reduced evaluation and transposition; returned proof steps 9

proof.text: Prove the generic closed identity-Hom comparison by injectivity of uncurry and the normalized identity tensorator square. Specialize it to finiteUnit. Use the successive-quotient cocycle already proved by finiteCoefficient_derivedHom_change for the other finite law.

Prove the generic composite-Hom comparison by uncurrying both paths, evaluation naturality and cancellation of the tensorator squares. Specialize to integral reduction followed by quotient reduction, using exactly integralAssoc and the tensor normalization square. No invertibility of the ambient Hom comparisons is used.

The elementary finite overlap is definitional equality. Choose a and the reduction presentations from the normalized integral evaluation lemma. Uncurry integralMap and comparison; the normalization identifies them by the closed bijection. Use comparison_isIso for invertibility.

Choose the jointly normalized ordinary presentations and e. The completion equation identifies each presentation completion isomorphism with e followed by scalarCompletionIso. Expand both completed Hom maps; factor the map on the two Hom arguments and use the ordinary Hom square. The two adjacent inverse e components cancel. The result is scalarHomCompleteInputs.hom, whose IsIso instance gives invertibility.

For finite quotients use the evaluation and compatibility conjuncts of finiteCoefficient_derivedHom_change. For integral reduction use the calculus finite_compatible field; prove evaluation existence and uniqueness directly from the closed bijection. For ordinary scalar extension use basicOperationsCoefficientReduction. The three associator laws are the tensor normalization lemma.

Use the raw rational Hom comparison and common-stage internal-Hom representative law supplied by basicOperationsCoefficientReduction, instantiated on the identity of X. Supply residue-field invertibility from the finite-field characteristic hypothesis. The three transport clauses follow by congrArg applied to the specified functor maps.
